precepts.why:
Isaiah tells Moab, “hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth”, and “Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler.” The outcast is us, the Israelites; that is why verse 1 speaks of “the mount of the daughter of Zion.” During the time of Nebuchadnezzar many Israelites fled and hid amongst Moab, and the spoiler they hid from was Nebuchadnezzar.

Jeremiah is the proof of where our people fled: “Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan.”

Where were they? In Moab, among the Ammonites, and in Edom. When the king of Babylon came through, Judah scattered into those lands and hid there, just as Isaiah told Moab to hide them. And “Sela” in verse 1 is Petra, which is Edom; they call Edom Petra today.

There is a dual meaning behind these scriptures. What happened with our people and Moab in the time of Nebuchadnezzar speaks again to the last days, when Moab is China and our people are outcasts among the nations, until “the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land” and the throne of Christ is established.

precepts.why:
“And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David.” The throne that is going to be established is the throne of Christ, and Isaiah 9 shows it: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” The government shall be upon the shoulders of Christ.

“and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” A lot of people don’t understand why he is called the everlasting Father. It is because the one you think is the heavenly Father in the Old Testament was actually Christ. That is why there is a lot of confusion in the Israelite community.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Don’t just read by that word increase; the mustard seed of Matthew 13 shows it. We are at the mustard seed stage now, and this is the beginning of God’s government.

“upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” To order it and establish it with judgment and justice: that is law and order. That is why we establish law, order and rank, and teach brothers and sisters the laws, commandments and statutes of the Holy Bible.

Some don’t like law because they like adultery better; they don’t like order because they like disorder, chaos, a toxic marriage and a chaotic life, married today and divorced tomorrow. That is genetic encoding from slavery, and it is in all of us. But the Bible can break that spirit, only if you let it. Only God can cleanse that from you, and his throne, established in mercy, is judging and “hasting righteousness.”

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof. We are at that mustard seed stage now. It did not end with Nat Turner; the history of the Israelite schools continues, and we here are part of that mustard seed that, when it is grown, is the greatest of all. All nations are going to submit to the King of kings.

precepts.why:
Isaiah 9:7 says, “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Why does it say the increase of his government? Christ answers in a parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.”

A mustard seed is one of the smallest of all seeds, and that is how the kingdom of heaven is on the earth now. “but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.” When it is grown is the increase. All nations are going to submit to it and follow what it says.

We are at that mustard seed stage now. A lot of people say that Israelite thing ain’t nothing. Oh no, it is something: it is the beginning of God’s government. And it is only going to increase. When you check the history from the time of Nat Turner, you might think it ended there. It did not. Look at the history of the Israelite schools; we here are part of that great history, part of that mustard seed that, when it is grown, is the greatest of all. You are not tricking us back into worshipping white Jesus.

So the throne of Isaiah 16:5, established in mercy in the tabernacle of David, starts small and grows until every nation lodges under it.

points: Send the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion, for the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon as a wandering bird cast out of the nest.

Moab is told to take counsel, execute judgment, make her shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday, hide the outcasts, and not betray the one that wanders. She is asked to be a covert to the outcasts from the face of the spoiler.

When the extortioner and spoiler are consumed out of the land, the throne shall be established in mercy, and one shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging and seeking judgment and hasting righteousness.
We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud, of his haughtiness and pride and wrath, but his lies shall not be so. Therefore Moab shall howl for Moab, everyone shall howl.

For the foundations of Kirhareseth they shall mourn, surely they are stricken. The fields of Heshbon languish and the vine of Sibmah, whose principal plants the lords of the heathen have broken down; her branches are stretched out, gone over the sea.
The prophet bewails the vine of Sibmah with weeping and waters Heshbon and Elealeh with his tears, for the shouting over the summer fruits and harvest is fallen.

Gladness and joy are taken away out of the plentiful field; in the vineyards there is no singing nor shouting, and the treaders tread out no wine in their presses, for the Most High has made the vintage shouting to cease.
The prophet's inward parts sound like a harp for Moab and for Kirharesh, and when Moab wearies himself upon the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, he shall not prevail.
This is the word the Most High has spoken concerning Moab since that time.

But now the Most High speaks, saying that within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be contemned with all that great multitude, and the remnant shall be very small and feeble.
